title: 美股周评 · 2026-10-10：防御未退，强势降温
title_en: U.S. Market Weekly Review · 2026-10-10: Defensive conditions persist, sector strength cools
subtitle: 结构压力延续，AI 硬件回落；长端利率仍构成约束
subtitle_en: Structural pressure persists as AI hardware cools; long-end rates remain a valuation constraint.
author: Taiyang Feng

## 本期判断：风险略缓，结构未解

截至 10 月 9 日，美股综合市场状态得分为 65.8，处于 Defensive / 防御。按本期同一重算版本，10 月 2 日为 66.59，10 月 9 日为 65.84，回落 0.75 点。风险有所缓和，但没有跨出防御区间；更不宜把这一小幅回落解释为风险已经解除。[1]

核心矛盾仍是市场内部结构：参与度风险 74.8、脆弱性 94.1，明显高于市场风险 54.5 与金融压力 40.0。少数资产保有趋势，并不等于市场整体已恢复广泛参与。金融条件暂未发出同等强度的压力信号，内部集中度与潜在同步调整风险仍更值得关注。[1]

AI 硬件综合分数由上期已发表的 91.5 降至本期 62.6，状态从 Strong 转为 Constructive。SMH 近 20 个交易日仍上涨 6.12%，近 5 日却下跌 4.32%。较长窗口中的相对强势与最近一周的降温同时成立，不能仅凭一个正的 20 日回报判断短期趋势没有变化。[1]

本期对决策的含义是保持选择性，而非全面恢复进攻。判断应同时参考整体参与、结构脆弱性、行业趋势与利率约束。周频模型显示的 Level 4 / 90% 是沿用信号，不能代替本周尚未生成的完整结果；参考风险敞口也不是作者或任何账户的实际仓位。[1]

## 市场结构：高脆弱性仍是主要约束

市场风险支柱为 54.5，处于谨慎；金融压力为 40.0，处于中性。与此同时，参与度风险仍处防御，脆弱性进入压力区间。当前更接近内部结构承压、金融压力尚未同步放大的状态，而不是所有风险来源都在同时恶化。[1]

综合状态反映四支柱的等权结果。参与度 74.8 与脆弱性 94.1 拉高综合值，即使另外两个支柱较低，整体仍留在防御区间。这解释了为什么部分指数或行业维持强势，并不足以自动推翻整体风险判断。[1]

本周同版本分数在 65.48 至 67.15 之间波动，10 月 9 日收于 65.84。低点仍位于防御阈值 65 上方；不能把区间内的波动称为状态切换。后续若分数下降，更需要观察参与度与脆弱性是否同步改善，而不只看综合值是否暂时跨过一条线。[1]

版本说明：上期已发表的 10 月 2 日读数为 66.82，本期重算历史中同日为 66.59。原报告保留其历史记录。本期周度比较采用同版本数据，避免把历史修订差异算作市场改善；旧版加权分数 58.4 也不与当前正式分数 65.8 混用。[1]

## 市场宽度与金融条件：需要分开读取

首页约 37% 的市场宽度不是单一的 200 日均线比例，而是 9 月末两项月度指标的简单平均：站上 200 日均线的比例 41.47%，过去 12 个月跑赢 SPY 基准代理的比例 32.60%，平均为 37.04%。该首页数值的观察日仍是 9 月 30 日。[1]

10 月 9 日的日度 200DMA 估计为 41.83%，对应 2,438 / 5,828 只有效样本。它与月度 37.04% 的定义、日期和分母不同，不能直接描述为宽度由 37% 升到 42%。综合状态中的参与度支柱使用最新日度均线广度，并结合仍截至 9 月末的 12 个月跑赢比例。[1]

NFCI 与 ANFCI 最新观察日为 10 月 2 日，分别为 -0.494 与 -0.504，差值为 0.010。NFCI 指向比历史平均水平宽松的金融条件；ANFCI 表明相对于当前经济环境也偏宽松。但近 4 周两项分别上升 0.066 与 0.086，意味着相对前期有所收紧。差值缩小本身不能证明整体金融条件进一步放松。[1][4]

因子拥挤度需要按版本与日期区分：9 月末的剔除市场因子多空版本为 0.732 / L3；8 月末的 beta 调整多头版本为 0.872 / L4。部分版本处于高位，与脆弱性读数一致，但这不是 10 月 9 日新生成的日频拥挤信号，也不支持笼统声称所有因子本周都变得更拥挤。[1]

## 半导体与 AI 硬件：建设性仍在，短期已回撤

AI 硬件状态为 62.6 / Constructive。需求动量 76.9、领导力宽度 72.0，仍提供支撑；供应链确认 58.8、相对风险偏好 57.6，则没有显示与上期同等强度的全面共振。建设性描述的是当前模型状态，不意味着后续价格必然上涨。[1]

在 28 只监测股票中，20 只站上 20 日均线，占 71.4%；22 只站上 50 日均线，占 78.6%。这两项衡量行业样本的短中期参与，与全市场的 200 日均线广度具有不同含义。行业内部仍有一定参与基础，但其覆盖范围与时间尺度需要明确区分。[1]

SMH 近 20 日比 SPY 高 4.25 个百分点，比 QQQ 高 1.03 个百分点，行业相对优势尚在。但近 5 日半导体 ETF 普遍下跌，而 SPY 上涨 1.16%、QQQ 上涨 0.23%，说明最近一周的强弱关系已经发生变化。[1][2]

拥挤与热度为 69.0，仍处 Elevated，较上期已发表的 81.5 有所回落，但尚未回到低风险状态。分化脆弱性为 52.5，状态为 Contained。趋势支撑减弱、热度缓解与部分风险仍抬升可以同时存在，需要分别观察各项变化，避免把行业降温等同于所有风险已经消失。[1]

## 行业内部：领导力与供应链并非整齐划一

近 20 日，AI 加速器样本平均上涨 7.98%，服务器与网络硬件上涨 7.39%，晶圆代工与设备上涨 6.36%，模拟、MCU 与功率上涨 2.89%，存储则下跌 3.78%。强势沿多个环节存在，但并非整个供应链同步上涨。[1]

近 5 日，服务器与网络硬件样本平均仍上涨 0.64%，其他四组则均下跌。AI 加速器下跌 3.31%，晶圆代工与设备下跌 6.11%，模拟、MCU 与功率下跌 6.19%，存储下跌 5.46%。短窗口中的降温比 20 日累计表现更明显。[1]

HPE、AMD 与 MRVL 是本期 20 日表现领先的监测股票，分别上涨约 18.3%、17.8% 与 16.6%。这一排序描述既有价格表现，不构成买入名单。领导者与其余股票的表现差异仍需与均线广度、供应链确认和风险热度一起判断。[1]

行业研究的关键在于区分强势延续与强势集中。如果相对收益仍为正，但宽度继续收缩、供应链确认减弱，那么行业强势可能越来越依赖少数领导者；若更多环节重新参与且热度受控，建设性状态才有更广泛的支持。以上是观察条件，不是对下周走势的预测。[1]

## 长端利率：窗口起点决定主导项

纽约联储 ACM 原始数据截至 10 月 8 日。10 年期拟合收益率为 5.217%，其中预期平均短端利率分项为 4.297%，期限溢价为 0.920%。两项之和构成拟合收益率；这是模型分解，不是当日实际成交的国债收益率报价。[1][3]

按截图选定的 21 个观测日间隔，即 9 月 9 日至 10 月 8 日，拟合收益率上升 39.48 bp：预期利率分项贡献 17.84 bp，期限溢价贡献 21.64 bp。在这个窗口，期限补偿上升的贡献更大，说明长端压力不能只归结为未来政策利率预期。[1][3]

过去一个自然月的起点是 9 月 8 日：合计上升 39.63 bp，其中预期分项贡献 23.23 bp，期限溢价贡献 16.40 bp。仅将起点提前一个观测日，主导项就不同。短窗口已经体现出期限补偿的压力，但不能将这个结论直接推广到自然月或所有期限；比较必须保持起止日一致。[1][3]

三个月、六个月与一年窗口中，预期利率分项贡献分别为 31.55、59.89 与 71.51 bp，均大于相应期限溢价贡献。长端利率上升继续构成估值约束，但其来源具有窗口依赖性；分解结果不是下一次 FOMC 决策的预测，也不能单独解释股票价格变化。[1][3]

## 下周观察：等待完整信号，关注共同确认

10 月 9 日周频风险信号仍处 PENDING_DATA。高收益信用利差序列 BAMLH0A0HYM2 最新到 10 月 8 日，未覆盖所需的周五观察。数据刷新请求成功不等于本周数据已齐全；本期不对缺失的 10 月 9 日信用变化作额外判断。[1][5]

页面显示的 Level 4 / 90% 沿用 10 月 2 日完整信号，生效日为 10 月 5 日。在信用数据补齐并完成计算前，无法判断 10 月 9 日新一周是否维持或改变该等级。较高参考敞口与整体 Defensive 状态并存，反映模型侧重不同，也要求结合参与度与脆弱性进行交叉验证。[1]

更积极的研究判断需要共同确认：综合状态风险下降，参与度与脆弱性同时缓解；日度均线广度改善且覆盖率稳定；AI 硬件的相对优势获得更多环节支持。反之，如果综合值重新上升、宽度进一步收缩或行业回撤扩大，则防御判断需要继续保留。[1]

利率与信用是独立的验证线索。观察长端利率变化由哪一分项推动，并保持窗口一致；等待高收益信用观察补齐，再检验其是否与其他压力指标同向。单个分数、单只强势股票或单次阈值跨越，都不足以替代这些交叉核对。

## 数据、方法、版本与披露

本期制作日期为 2026 年 10 月 10 日，主要股票及综合状态截至 10 月 9 日。各源并不同步：ACM 与高收益利差截至 10 月 8 日；NFCI / ANFCI 与沿用周频信号截至 10 月 2 日；月度宽度及多空拥挤截至 9 月 30 日；beta 调整多头拥挤截至 8 月 31 日。[1]

综合状态沿用现有四支柱模型：支柱采用仅使用此前历史的 5 年滚动分位，经足够历史预热后按四支柱等权合成。分数区间为 <35 建设性、35 至 <50 中性、50 至 <65 谨慎、65 至 <80 防御、≥80 压力。它不是危机概率；AI 硬件采用另一个模型，不能将两者分数视为同一尺度的风险值。[1]

价格变化使用 dashboard 的调整价格输入，未独立重建分红再投资回报，亦非策略回测收益。宽度采用 Massive 扩展数据与历史股票代码种子，并非官方 CRSP 当期覆盖；样本与分母可变。AI 硬件为 28 只监测股票，不代表完整行业。因子拥挤的不同版本不可互换。[1][2]

日期异常的独立 WQS 卡片标为 10 月 31 日，本期不将其数值作为已实现的当前观测。综合状态按冻结导出值报告，未重新估计。对历史读数修订、待补数据和不同观察窗口均单独标注；封面山景是品牌视觉，正文图表均由本期冻结输入生成。[1]

本材料由 Residual Inertia | 余势制作，作者 Taiyang Feng (Sunny)，用于独立研究与信息交流，不构成任何投资或证券交易建议。模型参考敞口不代表实际持仓；本期未提供作者持仓及利益冲突信息。历史表现与模型状态均不能保证未来结果。

因子拥挤度需要按版本与日期区分：9 月末的剔除市场因子多空版本为 0.732 / L3；8 月末的 beta 调整多头版本为 0.872 / L4。部分版本处于高位，与脆弱性读数一致，但这不是 10 月 9 日新生成的日频拥挤信号，也不支持笼统声称所有因子本周都变得更拥挤。[1]

## 半导体与 AI 硬件：建设性仍在，短期已回撤

AI 硬件状态为 62.6 / Constructive。需求动量 76.9、领导力宽度 72.0，仍提供支撑；供应链确认 58.8、相对风险偏好 57.6，则没有显示与上期同等强度的全面共振。建设性描述的是当前模型状态，不意味着后续价格必然上涨。[1]

在 28 只监测股票中，20 只站上 20 日均线，占 71.4%；22 只站上 50 日均线，占 78.6%。这两项衡量行业样本的短中期参与，与全市场的 200 日均线广度具有不同含义。行业内部仍有一定参与基础，但其覆盖范围与时间尺度需要明确区分。[1]

SMH 近 20 日比 SPY 高 4.25 个百分点，比 QQQ 高 1.03 个百分点，行业相对优势尚在。但近 5 日半导体 ETF 普遍下跌，而 SPY 上涨 1.16%、QQQ 上涨 0.23%，说明最近一周的强弱关系已经发生变化。[1][2]

拥挤与热度为 69.0，仍处 Elevated，较上期已发表的 81.5 有所回落，但尚未回到低风险状态。分化脆弱性为 52.5，状态为 Contained。趋势支撑减弱、热度缓解与部分风险仍抬升可以同时存在，需要分别观察各项变化，避免把行业降温等同于所有风险已经消失。[1]

## 行业内部：领导力与供应链并非整齐划一

近 20 日，AI 加速器样本平均上涨 7.98%，服务器与网络硬件上涨 7.39%，晶圆代工与设备上涨 6.36%，模拟、MCU 与功率上涨 2.89%，存储则下跌 3.78%。强势沿多个环节存在，但并非整个供应链同步上涨。[1]

近 5 日，服务器与网络硬件样本平均仍上涨 0.64%，其他四组则均下跌。AI 加速器下跌 3.31%，晶圆代工与设备下跌 6.11%，模拟、MCU 与功率下跌 6.19%，存储下跌 5.46%。短窗口中的降温比 20 日累计表现更明显。[1]

HPE、AMD 与 MRVL 是本期 20 日表现领先的监测股票，分别上涨约 18.3%、17.8% 与 16.6%。这一排序描述既有价格表现，不构成买入名单。领导者与其余股票的表现差异仍需与均线广度、供应链确认和风险热度一起判断。[1]

行业研究的关键在于区分强势延续与强势集中。如果相对收益仍为正，但宽度继续收缩、供应链确认减弱，那么行业强势可能越来越依赖少数领导者；若更多环节重新参与且热度受控，建设性状态才有更广泛的支持。以上是观察条件，不是对下周走势的预测。[1]

## 长端利率：窗口起点决定主导项

纽约联储 ACM 原始数据截至 10 月 8 日。10 年期拟合收益率为 5.217%，其中预期平均短端利率分项为 4.297%，期限溢价为 0.920%。两项之和构成拟合收益率；这是模型分解，不是当日实际成交的国债收益率报价。[1][3]

按截图选定的 21 个观测日间隔，即 9 月 9 日至 10 月 8 日，拟合收益率上升 39.48 bp：预期利率分项贡献 17.84 bp，期限溢价贡献 21.64 bp。在这个窗口，期限补偿上升的贡献更大，说明长端压力不能只归结为未来政策利率预期。[1][3]

过去一个自然月的起点是 9 月 8 日：合计上升 39.63 bp，其中预期分项贡献 23.23 bp，期限溢价贡献 16.40 bp。仅将起点提前一个观测日，主导项就不同。短窗口已经体现出期限补偿的压力，但不能将这个结论直接推广到自然月或所有期限；比较必须保持起止日一致。[1][3]

三个月、六个月与一年窗口中，预期利率分项贡献分别为 31.55、59.89 与 71.51 bp，均大于相应期限溢价贡献。长端利率上升继续构成估值约束，但其来源具有窗口依赖性；分解结果不是下一次 FOMC 决策的预测，也不能单独解释股票价格变化。[1][3]

## 下周观察：等待完整信号，关注共同确认

10 月 9 日周频风险信号仍处 PENDING_DATA。高收益信用利差序列 BAMLH0A0HYM2 最新到 10 月 8 日，未覆盖所需的周五观察。数据刷新请求成功不等于本周数据已齐全；本期不对缺失的 10 月 9 日信用变化作额外判断。[1][5]

页面显示的 Level 4 / 90% 沿用 10 月 2 日完整信号，生效日为 10 月 5 日。在信用数据补齐并完成计算前，无法判断 10 月 9 日新一周是否维持或改变该等级。较高参考敞口与整体 Defensive 状态并存，反映模型侧重不同，也要求结合参与度与脆弱性进行交叉验证。[1]

更积极的研究判断需要共同确认：综合状态风险下降，参与度与脆弱性同时缓解；日度均线广度改善且覆盖率稳定；AI 硬件的相对优势获得更多环节支持。反之，如果综合值重新上升、宽度进一步收缩或行业回撤扩大，则防御判断需要继续保留。[1]

利率与信用是独立的验证线索。观察长端利率变化由哪一分项推动，并保持窗口一致；等待高收益信用观察补齐，再检验其是否与其他压力指标同向。单个分数、单只强势股票或单次阈值跨越，都不足以替代这些交叉核对。

## 数据、方法、版本与披露

本期制作日期为 2026 年 10 月 10 日，主要股票及综合状态截至 10 月 9 日。各源并不同步：ACM 与高收益利差截至 10 月 8 日；NFCI / ANFCI 与沿用周频信号截至 10 月 2 日；月度宽度及多空拥挤截至 9 月 30 日；beta 调整多头拥挤截至 8 月 31 日。[1]

综合状态沿用现有四支柱模型：支柱采用仅使用此前历史的 5 年滚动分位，经足够历史预热后按四支柱等权合成。分数区间为 <35 建设性、35 至 <50 中性、50 至 <65 谨慎、65 至 <80 防御、≥80 压力。它不是危机概率；AI 硬件采用另一个模型，不能将两者分数视为同一尺度的风险值。[1]

价格变化使用 dashboard 的调整价格输入，未独立重建分红再投资回报，亦非策略回测收益。宽度采用 Massive 扩展数据与历史股票代码种子，并非官方 CRSP 当期覆盖；样本与分母可变。AI 硬件为 28 只监测股票，不代表完整行业。因子拥挤的不同版本不可互换。[1][2]

日期异常的独立 WQS 卡片标为 10 月 31 日，本期不将其数值作为已实现的当前观测。综合状态按冻结导出值报告，未重新估计。对历史读数修订、待补数据和不同观察窗口均单独标注；封面山景是品牌视觉，正文图表均由本期冻结输入生成。[1]

本材料由 Residual Inertia | 余势制作，作者 Taiyang Feng (Sunny)，用于独立研究与信息交流，不构成任何投资或证券交易建议。模型参考敞口不代表实际持仓；本期未提供作者持仓及利益冲突信息。历史表现与模型状态均不能保证未来结果。

## Risk eased slightly; the structure remains unresolved

As of October 9, the composite Market Regime score was 65.8, still Defensive. In the current data vintage, the October 2 score was 66.59 and the October 9 score was 65.84, a decline of 0.75 points. The reading improved slightly without leaving the Defensive range. This does not confirm that market risk has cleared.[1]

The main constraint remains internal structure. Participation risk at 74.8 and fragility at 94.1 are substantially higher than market risk at 54.5 and financial stress at 40.0. Persistent trends in selected assets do not establish broad participation across the market. Financial conditions have not produced the same intensity of pressure, while concentration and the potential for synchronized unwinds remain concerns.[1]

The AI hardware score declined from the previously published 91.5 to 62.6, changing from Strong to Constructive. SMH remained up 6.12% over 20 trading days but fell 4.32% over five days. Longer-window relative strength and recent cooling coexist; a positive 20-day return alone does not establish an unchanged short-term trend.[1]

The research interpretation remains selective rather than broadly aggressive. Participation, structural fragility, sector trends and rates should be considered together. The weekly model's Level 4 / 90% is a retained signal, not a completed new weekly reading. Reference exposure is not the author's or any account's actual allocation.[1]

## Market structure: fragility remains the main constraint

Market risk at 54.5 is Caution and financial stress at 40.0 is Neutral. Participation is still Defensive, while fragility is in Stress. This resembles internal structural pressure without a comparable amplification of financial stress, rather than simultaneous deterioration in every risk source.[1]

The composite is the equal-weighted result of four pillars. Participation at 74.8 and fragility at 94.1 keep the overall score elevated even with lower readings in the other two pillars. Strength in selected indexes or sectors therefore does not automatically invalidate the broad-market risk assessment.[1]

During the week, same-vintage composite readings ranged from 65.48 to 67.15 and ended at 65.84. Even the low remained above the Defensive threshold of 65. These fluctuations are not state changes. Any future decline should be assessed alongside participation and fragility, not solely a temporary threshold crossing.[1]

The previous report retains its originally published October 2 reading of 66.82; the current recalculated history reports 66.59 for that date. Weekly comparisons here use one vintage so revisions are not treated as market improvement. The legacy weighted reading of 58.4 uses a different methodology and is not interchangeable with the current official reading of 65.8.[1]

## Breadth and financial conditions require separate readings

The dashboard's approximately 37% breadth figure is not a single 200-day moving-average ratio. It is the simple mean of two September month-end measures: 41.47% above the 200-day average and 32.60% outperforming the SPY benchmark proxy over 12 months. Their mean is 37.04%, with an observation date of September 30.[1]

The October 9 daily 200DMA estimate is 41.83%, or 2,438 of 5,828 eligible observations. Its definition, date and denominator differ from the monthly composite, so this cannot be described as breadth rising from 37% to 42%. The regime's participation pillar combines the latest daily moving-average breadth with the September month-end 12-month outperform ratio.[1]

NFCI and ANFCI observations dated October 2 were -0.494 and -0.504, with a difference of 0.010. NFCI indicates conditions looser than their historical average; ANFCI indicates conditions looser than expected given the current economic environment. However, their four-week changes were +0.066 and +0.086, indicating tightening relative to earlier readings. A narrower gap does not by itself establish further overall easing.[1][4]

Factor crowding is version- and date-specific. The September month-end long-short variant excluding the market factor was 0.732 / L3. The August month-end beta-adjusted long-only variant was 0.872 / L4. Elevated readings in selected variants are consistent with fragility, but they are not new October 9 daily signals and do not establish that every factor became more crowded this week.[1]

## Semiconductors and AI hardware: constructive, with a recent pullback

AI hardware scored 62.6, Constructive. Demand momentum at 76.9 and leadership breadth at 72.0 still provide support. Supply-chain confirmation at 58.8 and relative risk appetite at 57.6 do not show the same degree of broad reinforcement as the prior report. Constructive describes the model state, not a guarantee of subsequent gains.[1]

Of 28 monitored stocks, 20 were above their 20-day moving averages (71.4%) and 22 above their 50-day averages (78.6%). These measure short- and medium-term participation in the sector sample, with a different universe and horizon from broad-market 200DMA breadth.[1]

SMH's 20-day return exceeded SPY's by 4.25 percentage points and QQQ's by 1.03 percentage points. Relative advantage remained, but semiconductor ETFs generally declined over five days while SPY gained 1.16% and QQQ gained 0.23%. The recent week's relative performance therefore differs from the longer window.[1][2]

Crowding/heat was 69.0, Elevated, below the prior published 81.5 but not back to a low-risk state. Divergence fragility was 52.5, Contained. Weaker trend support, cooler heat and residual elevated risks can coexist. Sector cooling should not be equated with the disappearance of every risk.[1]

## Sector internals: leadership and supply-chain performance differ

Over 20 trading days, monitored AI accelerators gained an average 7.98%, servers and networking gained 7.39%, foundry and equipment gained 6.36%, and analog/MCU/power gained 2.89%. Memory and storage fell 3.78%. Strength exists across multiple parts of the chain, but participation is uneven.[1]

Over five days, servers and networking still gained 0.64% on average; all four other groups declined. AI accelerators fell 3.31%, foundry and equipment 6.11%, analog/MCU/power 6.19%, and memory/storage 5.46%. Cooling is more evident in this short window than in cumulative 20-day returns.[1]

HPE, AMD and MRVL led the monitored universe over 20 days, gaining approximately 18.3%, 17.8% and 16.6%. This is a ranking of observed price changes, not a buy list. The difference between leaders and other stocks should be considered with breadth, supply-chain confirmation and risk heat.[1]

If relative returns stay positive while breadth contracts and supply-chain confirmation weakens, sector strength may depend increasingly on a few leaders. Renewed participation across more groups, with controlled heat, would provide broader support for a Constructive reading. These are observation conditions, not predictions for next week.[1]

## Long-term rates: the start date changes the dominant contribution

The New York Fed ACM source is available through October 8. The 10-year fitted yield was 5.217%, comprising an expected-average-short-rate component of 4.297% and a term premium of 0.920%. The components sum to the fitted yield. This is a model decomposition, not a traded Treasury yield quote.[1][3]

Across 21 observation intervals, September 9 to October 8, the fitted yield rose 39.48 basis points: 17.84 bp from expected rates and 21.64 bp from the term premium. In that window, rising term compensation contributed more, so long-end pressure cannot be attributed exclusively to policy-rate expectations.[1][3]

The calendar-month window starts September 8: the total increase was 39.63 bp, comprising 23.23 bp from expected rates and 16.40 bp from the premium. Moving the start date back one observation changes the dominant component. Short-window term compensation pressure cannot be generalized to the calendar month or every horizon; comparisons must preserve their dates.[1][3]

Over three months, six months and one year, expected-rate contributions were 31.55, 59.89 and 71.51 bp, respectively, exceeding the corresponding premium contributions. Rising long-end rates remain a valuation constraint, with window-dependent drivers. This decomposition is neither a forecast of the next FOMC decision nor a standalone explanation of equity prices.[1][3]

## Next observations: wait for a complete signal and seek joint confirmation

The October 9 weekly risk signal remains PENDING_DATA. The high-yield spread input BAMLH0A0HYM2 currently ends October 8, short of the required Friday observation. A successful refresh request does not mean the week's inputs are complete. No additional assessment of missing October 9 credit-market changes is made here.[1][5]

Displayed Level 4 / 90% retains the complete October 2 signal, effective October 5. Whether the new October 9 week maintains or changes that level cannot be established until credit data is complete and calculations are finished. Higher reference exposure coexisting with a Defensive composite reflects different model emphases and requires cross-checking participation and fragility.[1]

A more positive research assessment requires joint confirmation: lower composite risk alongside easing participation risk and fragility, improved daily moving-average breadth with stable coverage, and AI hardware relative strength supported by more groups. Renewed composite increases, narrower breadth or a wider sector pullback would support retaining the Defensive assessment.[1]

Rates and credit provide separate checks. Track which component drives long-end yield changes using consistent windows, and wait for the missing high-yield observation before assessing alignment with other stress indicators. A single score, strong stock or threshold crossing does not substitute for these checks.

## Data, methodology, versions and disclosure

Published October 10, 2026. Equity and composite observations mainly run through October 9. ACM and high-yield spread observations end October 8; NFCI/ANFCI and the retained weekly signal end October 2; monthly breadth and long-short crowding end September 30; beta-adjusted long-only crowding ends August 31.[1]

The existing composite model uses four equally weighted pillars based on prior-only five-year rolling percentiles after sufficient history. Ranges are below 35 Constructive, 35 to below 50 Neutral, 50 to below 65 Caution, 65 to below 80 Defensive, and 80 or above Stress. These are not crisis probabilities. AI hardware uses a separate model, so its score is not the same risk scale.[1]

Price changes use dashboard adjusted-price inputs; dividend-reinvestment returns were not independently reconstructed, and results are not strategy performance. Breadth uses the Massive extension with historical ticker seeds, not official current CRSP coverage; eligible samples and denominators vary. The AI universe contains 28 monitored stocks, not the entire sector. Crowding variants are not interchangeable.[1][2]

The standalone WQS card labeled October 31 is not treated as a realized current observation. The exported composite is retained without re-estimation. Revisions, pending data and different windows are identified separately. Cover mountains are brand imagery; report charts use frozen inputs.[1]

Prepared by Residual Inertia | 余势, author Taiyang Feng (Sunny), for independent research and information sharing. This is not investment or securities-trading advice. Model reference exposure is not actual holdings; the report does not provide the author's holdings or conflicts of interest. Historical results and model states do not guarantee future outcomes.

## Market structure: fragility remains the main constraint

Market risk at 54.5 is Caution and financial stress at 40.0 is Neutral. Participation is still Defensive, while fragility is in Stress. This resembles internal structural pressure without a comparable amplification of financial stress, rather than simultaneous deterioration in every risk source.[1]

The composite is the equal-weighted result of four pillars. Participation at 74.8 and fragility at 94.1 keep the overall score elevated even with lower readings in the other two pillars. Strength in selected indexes or sectors therefore does not automatically invalidate the broad-market risk assessment.[1]

During the week, same-vintage composite readings ranged from 65.48 to 67.15 and ended at 65.84. Even the low remained above the Defensive threshold of 65. These fluctuations are not state changes. Any future decline should be assessed alongside participation and fragility, not solely a temporary threshold crossing.[1]

The previous report retains its originally published October 2 reading of 66.82; the current recalculated history reports 66.59 for that date. Weekly comparisons here use one vintage so revisions are not treated as market improvement. The legacy weighted reading of 58.4 uses a different methodology and is not interchangeable with the current official reading of 65.8.[1]

## Breadth and financial conditions require separate readings

The dashboard's approximately 37% breadth figure is not a single 200-day moving-average ratio. It is the simple mean of two September month-end measures: 41.47% above the 200-day average and 32.60% outperforming the SPY benchmark proxy over 12 months. Their mean is 37.04%, with an observation date of September 30.[1]

The October 9 daily 200DMA estimate is 41.83%, or 2,438 of 5,828 eligible observations. Its definition, date and denominator differ from the monthly composite, so this cannot be described as breadth rising from 37% to 42%. The regime's participation pillar combines the latest daily moving-average breadth with the September month-end 12-month outperform ratio.[1]

NFCI and ANFCI observations dated October 2 were -0.494 and -0.504, with a difference of 0.010. NFCI indicates conditions looser than their historical average; ANFCI indicates conditions looser than expected given the current economic environment. However, their four-week changes were +0.066 and +0.086, indicating tightening relative to earlier readings. A narrower gap does not by itself establish further overall easing.[1][4]

Factor crowding is version- and date-specific. The September month-end long-short variant excluding the market factor was 0.732 / L3. The August month-end beta-adjusted long-only variant was 0.872 / L4. Elevated readings in selected variants are consistent with fragility, but they are not new October 9 daily signals and do not establish that every factor became more crowded this week.[1]

## Semiconductors and AI hardware: constructive, with a recent pullback

AI hardware scored 62.6, Constructive. Demand momentum at 76.9 and leadership breadth at 72.0 still provide support. Supply-chain confirmation at 58.8 and relative risk appetite at 57.6 do not show the same degree of broad reinforcement as the prior report. Constructive describes the model state, not a guarantee of subsequent gains.[1]

Of 28 monitored stocks, 20 were above their 20-day moving averages (71.4%) and 22 above their 50-day averages (78.6%). These measure short- and medium-term participation in the sector sample, with a different universe and horizon from broad-market 200DMA breadth.[1]

SMH's 20-day return exceeded SPY's by 4.25 percentage points and QQQ's by 1.03 percentage points. Relative advantage remained, but semiconductor ETFs generally declined over five days while SPY gained 1.16% and QQQ gained 0.23%. The recent week's relative performance therefore differs from the longer window.[1][2]

Crowding/heat was 69.0, Elevated, below the prior published 81.5 but not back to a low-risk state. Divergence fragility was 52.5, Contained. Weaker trend support, cooler heat and residual elevated risks can coexist. Sector cooling should not be equated with the disappearance of every risk.[1]

## Sector internals: leadership and supply-chain performance differ

Over 20 trading days, monitored AI accelerators gained an average 7.98%, servers and networking gained 7.39%, foundry and equipment gained 6.36%, and analog/MCU/power gained 2.89%. Memory and storage fell 3.78%. Strength exists across multiple parts of the chain, but participation is uneven.[1]

Over five days, servers and networking still gained 0.64% on average; all four other groups declined. AI accelerators fell 3.31%, foundry and equipment 6.11%, analog/MCU/power 6.19%, and memory/storage 5.46%. Cooling is more evident in this short window than in cumulative 20-day returns.[1]

HPE, AMD and MRVL led the monitored universe over 20 days, gaining approximately 18.3%, 17.8% and 16.6%. This is a ranking of observed price changes, not a buy list. The difference between leaders and other stocks should be considered with breadth, supply-chain confirmation and risk heat.[1]

If relative returns stay positive while breadth contracts and supply-chain confirmation weakens, sector strength may depend increasingly on a few leaders. Renewed participation across more groups, with controlled heat, would provide broader support for a Constructive reading. These are observation conditions, not predictions for next week.[1]

## Long-term rates: the start date changes the dominant contribution

The New York Fed ACM source is available through October 8. The 10-year fitted yield was 5.217%, comprising an expected-average-short-rate component of 4.297% and a term premium of 0.920%. The components sum to the fitted yield. This is a model decomposition, not a traded Treasury yield quote.[1][3]

Across 21 observation intervals, September 9 to October 8, the fitted yield rose 39.48 basis points: 17.84 bp from expected rates and 21.64 bp from the term premium. In that window, rising term compensation contributed more, so long-end pressure cannot be attributed exclusively to policy-rate expectations.[1][3]

The calendar-month window starts September 8: the total increase was 39.63 bp, comprising 23.23 bp from expected rates and 16.40 bp from the premium. Moving the start date back one observation changes the dominant component. Short-window term compensation pressure cannot be generalized to the calendar month or every horizon; comparisons must preserve their dates.[1][3]

Over three months, six months and one year, expected-rate contributions were 31.55, 59.89 and 71.51 bp, respectively, exceeding the corresponding premium contributions. Rising long-end rates remain a valuation constraint, with window-dependent drivers. This decomposition is neither a forecast of the next FOMC decision nor a standalone explanation of equity prices.[1][3]

## Next observations: wait for a complete signal and seek joint confirmation

The October 9 weekly risk signal remains PENDING_DATA. The high-yield spread input BAMLH0A0HYM2 currently ends October 8, short of the required Friday observation. A successful refresh request does not mean the week's inputs are complete. No additional assessment of missing October 9 credit-market changes is made here.[1][5]

Displayed Level 4 / 90% retains the complete October 2 signal, effective October 5. Whether the new October 9 week maintains or changes that level cannot be established until credit data is complete and calculations are finished. Higher reference exposure coexisting with a Defensive composite reflects different model emphases and requires cross-checking participation and fragility.[1]

A more positive research assessment requires joint confirmation: lower composite risk alongside easing participation risk and fragility, improved daily moving-average breadth with stable coverage, and AI hardware relative strength supported by more groups. Renewed composite increases, narrower breadth or a wider sector pullback would support retaining the Defensive assessment.[1]

Rates and credit provide separate checks. Track which component drives long-end yield changes using consistent windows, and wait for the missing high-yield observation before assessing alignment with other stress indicators. A single score, strong stock or threshold crossing does not substitute for these checks.

## Data, methodology, versions and disclosure

Published October 10, 2026. Equity and composite observations mainly run through October 9. ACM and high-yield spread observations end October 8; NFCI/ANFCI and the retained weekly signal end October 2; monthly breadth and long-short crowding end September 30; beta-adjusted long-only crowding ends August 31.[1]

The existing composite model uses four equally weighted pillars based on prior-only five-year rolling percentiles after sufficient history. Ranges are below 35 Constructive, 35 to below 50 Neutral, 50 to below 65 Caution, 65 to below 80 Defensive, and 80 or above Stress. These are not crisis probabilities. AI hardware uses a separate model, so its score is not the same risk scale.[1]

Price changes use dashboard adjusted-price inputs; dividend-reinvestment returns were not independently reconstructed, and results are not strategy performance. Breadth uses the Massive extension with historical ticker seeds, not official current CRSP coverage; eligible samples and denominators vary. The AI universe contains 28 monitored stocks, not the entire sector. Crowding variants are not interchangeable.[1][2]

The standalone WQS card labeled October 31 is not treated as a realized current observation. The exported composite is retained without re-estimation. Revisions, pending data and different windows are identified separately. Cover mountains are brand imagery; report charts use frozen inputs.[1]
